title: Pilot Outage / No Pilot
shortDescription: Gas valve does not detect pilot flame.
fullDescription:
On State gas water heaters, a single LED flash on the gas control valve indicates pilot outage — the thermopile is not generating enough millivolts to keep the pilot valve open.

Most commonly the thermopile has weakened with age, or the pilot orifice is clogged with dust or spider webs (FVIR units especially).
safetyWarning: If you smell gas, do not light. Ventilate and call gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas supply
fixSteps.instruction: Check manual gas valve open and other appliances work.

fixSteps.title: Test thermopile
fixSteps.instruction: Measure millivolts at gas valve TH-TP terminals; should be 600-800mV.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if pilot will not stay lit after thermopile swap.

title: Pilot Will Not Light / Gas Valve Fault
shortDescription: Pilot ignition attempted but no flame detected.
fullDescription: Two flashes mean the pilot did not light during the ignition attempt. Causes include no gas, blocked orifice, or failed igniter on power-vent models.
safetyWarning: Ventilate before retrying ignition.

fixSteps.title: Purge gas line
fixSteps.instruction: If recently shut off, hold pilot button longer to bleed air.

fixSteps.title: Clean pilot assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum FVIR air intake screen and pilot tube.

whenToCallPro: If pilot still will not light.

title: Thermopile / Thermocouple Voltage Low
shortDescription: Thermopile output below operating threshold.
fullDescription: Three flashes warn the thermopile millivolt output is below the gas valve hold-in threshold. Pilot may light but burner may not stay on.
whenToCallPro: If new thermopile does not help.

title: Tank Temperature Exceeds Limit
shortDescription: Tank water exceeded high-limit threshold.
fullDescription:
Four flashes indicate the tank temperature sensor read above the safety limit (typically 190F). Gas valve will lock out.

Possible causes: failed gas valve, scale buildup, or thermostat failure.
safetyWarning: Hot water can scald. Allow tank to cool before service.

fixSteps.title: Allow cooldown
fixSteps.instruction: Let tank cool 1 hour before reset.

fixSteps.title: Replace gas valve
fixSteps.instruction: OEM matched valve, requires gas leak test.

title: Sensor Failure
shortDescription: Tank temperature sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: Five flashes mean the tank temperature sensor input is invalid. On most State models the sensor is integrated with the gas valve.

title: Combustion Air Blocked / FVIR Trip
shortDescription: Air intake screen blocked or vapor sensor tripped.
fullDescription: Six flashes on FVIR-equipped State water heaters indicate the combustion air screen is blocked with lint and dust, or the vapor sensor detected flammable vapors.
safetyWarning: Never store gasoline or solvents near a gas water heater.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum air screen
fixSteps.instruction: Use vacuum on bottom intake screen of tank.

fixSteps.title: Remove vapor sources
fixSteps.instruction: Move paint, gasoline, solvents away from heater.

title: Gas Valve Internal Failure
shortDescription: Electronic gas control board fault.
fullDescription: Seven flashes indicate the integrated gas control board has an internal failure. The valve must be replaced.
safetyWarning: Gas valve work requires leak testing.

faq.a: State often covers 6-10 years on parts.

title: Electric Element Open / Failed
shortDescription: Heating element has failed open.
fullDescription: On State electric tank water heaters with digital control, E1 indicates an open heating element. Tank scale and burnout from dry-firing are common causes.
safetyWarning: Turn off breaker before service. 240V can be lethal.
symptoms: No hot water (one element) or lukewarm only

fixSteps.title: Test elements
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; measure resistance — open circuit means failure.

fixSteps.title: Replace element
fixSteps.instruction: Drain tank, swap element, refill before powering up.

whenToCallPro: If unfamiliar with 240V wiring or draining tank.

title: ECO / High Limit Trip
shortDescription: Energy cutoff tripped due to overheat.
fullDescription: E2 indicates the ECO (Energy Cut Off) on the upper thermostat tripped because tank water exceeded ~170F. Usually caused by a stuck thermostat.
safetyWarning: Hot water hazard; allow tank to cool.

fixSteps.title: Press reset button
fixSteps.instruction: Red ECO reset on upper thermostat assembly.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: If trips repeatedly, swap upper thermostat.

title: No Ignition (Tankless)
shortDescription: Tankless unit failed to ignite.
fullDescription: Code 11 on State tankless gas water heaters means no ignition was detected. Causes include closed gas valve, low gas pressure, or air in line on initial install.
safetyWarning: Check for gas odor before retry.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm valve fully open and other appliances work.

fixSteps.title: Reset and retry
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle to retry ignition; allow line to bleed.

fixSteps.title: Check gas line size
fixSteps.instruction: Tankless needs 3/4 in. supply for most BTU ratings.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if gas pressure or line size issue.

faq.a: Larger gas line and dedicated venting.

title: Combustion Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
shortDescription: The combustion pressure switch is closed when the fan is off.
fullDescription: State (rebadged AO Smith) error 8F indicates the combustion pressure switch did not open at fan-off, suggesting a stuck switch or wiring short. The unit will lock out for safety.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: If the code persists, switch replacement is required.

faq.a: No — never bypass a vent-safety device.
Aging diaphragms can stick over time.

title: Inducer Fan Underspeed
shortDescription: Combustion fan is not reaching required RPM.
fullDescription: Error 9F indicates the inducer fan is below commanded speed. Dust buildup, bearing wear, or PCB drive failure are typical causes.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: If cleaning does not resolve, fan replacement is needed.

faq.q: How often should I clean the fan?
Are State and AO Smith the same?
faq.a: State is a brand of AO Smith; many parts cross-reference.

title: Outdoor Air Sensor Open
shortDescription: Hybrid heat pump outdoor air sensor reads open circuit.
fullDescription: On State hybrid heat pump models, error 10F indicates the ambient air sensor has failed. The unit defaults to electric mode.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: Sensor replacement is straightforward; reference the model service manual.

faq.q: Will I still have hot water?

faq.a: Heat pump mode is 2-3x more efficient.

title: Anode Current Fault
shortDescription: Powered anode current is out of range.
fullDescription: Error 12F on State indicates the powered anode current measurement is anomalous, often due to an empty tank or failed anode.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Verify Tank Full
fixSteps.instruction: Open a hot tap; let water flow steadily.

faq.q: How long do powered anodes last?

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Display and main board communication failure.
fullDescription: State error E3 indicates a communication fault between the user interface and main control board. Reseat ribbon connectors first.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat the display ribbon.

title: Outlet Hi-Limit Open
shortDescription: Outlet thermal hi-limit switch open.
fullDescription: Error E4 indicates the mechanical outlet hi-limit is open due to overheat conditions. Address scaling and flow first.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: If recurring, the hi-limit switch may be failed.

title: Inducer Fan Stalled
shortDescription: The inducer fan has stopped during operation.
fullDescription: Error E5 indicates a mid-operation fan stall — usually from worn bearings or sudden obstruction.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; check for foreign objects.

faq.a: No — fan is critical for venting safety.
Failures rise after 8-10 years of use.

title: Heat Pump Compressor Fault
shortDescription: Heat pump compressor protection has activated.
fullDescription: On State hybrid heat pump models, E6 reports a compressor protection event — often from low refrigerant, high head pressure, or thermal overload.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Clean Air Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean / replace the heat pump air filter.

faq.a: No — federal law restricts refrigerant handling.

title: Pressure Sensor Out of Range
shortDescription: Combustion or system pressure sensor reads abnormal value.
fullDescription: State error E7 indicates the pressure sensor output is out of range, suggesting a sensor or tubing failure.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Tubing
fixSteps.instruction: Verify pressure tube routing and condition.

faq.a: Different fault types — E7 is sensor analog, 7F is switch state.

title: EEPROM Memory Fault
shortDescription: Control board EEPROM has failed self-test.
fullDescription: Error E8 indicates the PCB nonvolatile memory may be corrupted. A long power cycle is the first remedy; if that fails, board replacement is needed.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before any internal work. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas utility.
whenToCallPro: Board replacement and reconfiguration is a technician task.

faq.q: Should I add a surge protector?

faq.a: Possibly — they may revert to defaults.

title: Stack Limit Open
shortDescription: Vent stack high-limit opened.
fullDescription: State Water code 13F indicates the stack high-temperature limit opened. Causes mirror those of similar tankless brands: scaled heat exchanger or vent restriction.

fixSteps.title: Cool Down
fixSteps.instruction: Wait for unit to cool fully.

whenToCallPro: Persistent 13F after descale and venting check requires a technician.

title: Recirculation Pump Fault
shortDescription: Internal recirc pump not running.
fullDescription: State Water 14F indicates the recirc pump did not start when commanded. Seized impeller or failed motor are typical.

title: Air Filter Dirty
shortDescription: Air intake filter requires cleaning.
fullDescription: Code 15F is a service notice — clean the intake air filter.
whenToCallPro: If 15F returns immediately, the air-flow sensor may be misreading — call a technician.

title: Inlet Thermistor Open
shortDescription: Cold inlet thermistor reads open.
fullDescription: Code 16F: open inlet thermistor circuit; reseat or replace the sensor.
whenToCallPro: If sensor measures good, call a technician.

title: Inlet Thermistor Short
shortDescription: Cold inlet thermistor reads short.
fullDescription: Code 17F: short on inlet thermistor circuit. Inspect connector for moisture and replace sensor if necessary.
whenToCallPro: Persistent short indicates harness damage; call a technician.

title: Outlet Thermistor Open
shortDescription: Hot outlet thermistor reads open.
fullDescription: Code 18F: open outlet thermistor circuit. Reseat or replace.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, call a technician.

title: Outlet Thermistor Short
shortDescription: Hot outlet thermistor reads short.
fullDescription: Code 19F: short on outlet thermistor circuit. Inspect harness and replace sensor.
whenToCallPro: Persistent short means wiring damage — call a technician.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Display-to-PCB communication lost.
fullDescription: Code 20F means display and main board are not communicating. Reseat the ribbon cable; if that fails, replacement is required.
whenToCallPro: If reseating fails, call a technician for parts replacement.

title: Maintenance Required
shortDescription: Annual service interval reached.
fullDescription: Code E9 is a service reminder. Schedule descaling and inspection, then reset.
whenToCallPro: If preferred, call a plumber for annual service.

title: Cold Water Sandwich Detected
shortDescription: Repeated short cycles producing temperature sandwich.
fullDescription: Code E10 is a warning that the unit detected cold-water-sandwich behavior — repeated short on/off cycles where cold slugs interrupt hot delivery. Common in installations without a recirc loop.

fixSteps.title: Add Recirc Buffer
fixSteps.instruction: Consider adding a small buffer tank or recirc loop.

title: Hot Surface Igniter Open
shortDescription: Hot surface igniter element measured open circuit.
fullDescription: Code 21F on State commercial water heaters indicates the hot surface igniter element measured as an open circuit during the pre-purge check.
safetyWarning: Igniter operates at high temperature - allow to cool before service.

fixSteps.title: Replace Igniter
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new hot surface igniter.

whenToCallPro: If terminals are good and a new igniter does not solve it, hire a pro.

title: Inducer Pressure Switch Stuck Open
shortDescription: Inducer pressure switch did not close on call for heat.
fullDescription: Code 22F indicates the pressure switch did not close when the inducer fan started. Without flow proof, the unit cannot ignite.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass pressure switches - they prevent flue gas spillage.

fixSteps.title: Check Tube
fixSteps.instruction: Verify pressure tube is connected and dry.

whenToCallPro: If vent is clear and tube is good, switch test needs a pro.

faq.a: It proves draft before allowing gas to flow.

title: Inducer Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
shortDescription: Inducer pressure switch closed before inducer started.
fullDescription: Code 23F indicates the pressure switch was already closed at startup, suggesting a stuck switch or a stuck contact.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass safety switches.

fixSteps.title: Schedule Service
fixSteps.instruction: Call a tech to test the switch and wiring.

faq.q: Can I just replace the switch?
faq.a: Possible, but the wiring should be tested first.

title: Flame Rollout Switch Tripped
shortDescription: Flame rollout safety switch tripped.
fullDescription: Code 24F indicates the flame rollout switch detected flame outside the combustion chamber. This is a critical safety event.
safetyWarning: DANGER: Flame rollout indicates a potentially blocked vent or heat exchanger. Shut off gas immediately.

fixSteps.title: Shut Off Gas
fixSteps.instruction: Close gas shutoff to the unit.

whenToCallPro: Always - this is a safety lockout.

faq.a: Yes, very. Carbon monoxide risk - always call a pro.

title: Flue Sensor Open
shortDescription: Flue temperature sensor open circuit.
fullDescription: Code 25F indicates the flue temperature sensor circuit is open. The unit cannot monitor combustion temperature.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Re-seat flue sensor at the control board.

whenToCallPro: Reach into the flue can be tight; pros may be faster.

faq.a: To detect heat exchanger fouling or vent blockage.

title: Flue Sensor Short
shortDescription: Flue temperature sensor shorted.
fullDescription: Code 26F indicates the flue thermistor reads as a short, often due to wire damage from heat.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check for chafing or melted insulation near the flue.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new flue thermistor with high-temp wiring.

whenToCallPro: If wiring routing needs rework, a pro is recommended.

faq.q: Can the flue get too hot?
faq.a: Yes, if heat exchanger is fouled, flue temps spike.

title: Flame Sense Out of Range
shortDescription: Flame current outside expected range.
fullDescription: Code 27F indicates flame rectification current is outside the normal operating window. The flame is present but signal quality is poor.

fixSteps.title: Clean Flame Rod
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean the flame rod with fine sandpaper.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning does not solve it, schedule a pro.

title: Cold Junction Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Internal cold junction reference sensor fault.
fullDescription: Code 28F indicates the cold junction reference inside the controller is reading out of range. Affects accuracy of thermocouple readings.

fixSteps.title: Replace Board
fixSteps.instruction: Have control board replaced if fault recurs.

whenToCallPro: Internal sensor faults usually require board replacement.

faq.a: Yes - mechanical rooms above 120F can stress controls.

title: Inducer Speed Out of Range
shortDescription: Inducer fan speed outside commanded range.
fullDescription: Code 29F indicates the inducer fan motor speed feedback does not match commanded RPM.
whenToCallPro: Inducer replacement is a pro task.

faq.a: Sometimes, but fault may recur during operation.

title: Anti-Scald Thermistor Fault
shortDescription: Anti-scald outlet sensor reading invalid.
fullDescription: Code 30F indicates the anti-scald outlet thermistor is reading out of range, disabling anti-scald protection.
safetyWarning: Anti-scald inactive - water may be hotter than set point until repaired.
whenToCallPro: If access is poor, hire a pro.

faq.a: Usually limits outlet to 120F per code.
